title: We built a turkey out of Gaussian splats and made it run for its life
author: Vegetable_Builder236
selftext:
We made a free Thanksgiving browser game where you’re a turkey trying to survive seven days on the farm. Since you spend most of the game staring at the turkey’s butt, the tail got a surprising amount of attention.

The bird is built in code. Around 1,500 little colored splats follow the curve of its body like feathers. The tail is a separate fan with two overlapping rows, 16 feathers behind 17, each with a dark band and a pale tip. The head and legs have their own pivots so the bird can bob its head, run and duck under things.

We used the same splat renderer for the farmer, pumpkins and hay bales. The wooden fences and metal axe blades are regular 3D meshes, so they keep a sharp edge even when the rest of the farm looks soft.

One part of our AI workflow was comparing two views of the same bird. Claude played the browser build and captured a close-up where you can see the feather bands. Codex recorded the run attached here. From the chase camera, I mostly notice the outline of the whole fan. If you’ve animated a splat character, what details actually held up once you pulled the camera back?

You can play it here: https://thearcadeshelf.com/turkey-escape/turkey-escape.html
